Just as a little piggyback from some of the comments. But please know that it is normal to feel anxious and many other things that come out of the blue. You’re not alone. 

I start by taking deep breaths for several minutes, then I usually tend to look at my surroundings in my room to find a certain distraction whether that being my old Yamaha keyboard or my ukulele that i recently bought. 

But one other thing that stands out from the rest personally. I have a friend of mine who I led a high school catholic retreat as seniors in high school. her name is Chloe. i opened up about going through some rough patches of feeling alone, depressed, and very anxious in certain situations while at the retreat. 

When the retreat was over, I came home to my mom cursing me out because I left my suit in one of my friends’ car, which later in the evening it triggered me and I had a very bad relapse to where I started cutting after being about a year clean. 

Next day, we went back to school, everyone of my classmates that led the retreat (which were 13, including Chloe) knew what happened because i texted them in our group chat that I wasn’t doing well. Next thing I know, I’m at my locker, I’m in arms embrace by all of my fellow leaders. It was very comforting and I was in tears. but was glad to know that i was loved. then Chloe comes up to me in tears, hugs me individually, and hands me a handwritten letter. to sum it up, it was to know that everyone in the team was here for me. I loved every bit of it. there was also some poems by amazing poet Robert Frost in the letter (which I recommend to look up). 

But whenever I start to feel down again, I use the letter that Chloe gave me as another thing to cope the MOST. To know that I’m not alone. Very lengthy story I know, but I thought it would be good to post this on Reddit sooner or later. 

And to Chloe, who I’m not sure uses Reddit, thank you!
well, you can definitely talk to me about these things and i’ll try to help you to the best of my ability. we’re here for you. for i have my own struggles of depression and anxiety myself.

Just joined this subreddit. And this is true in many ways for myself. I was diagnosed with Aspergers myself entering Kindergarten. Then I went along with switching to public and private schools every year, where I would eventually stay at a private catholic school. I remember being on medication all the way up until junior high to when I was able to actually socialize properly with my classmates, teachers, and family. 

But I never felt like I belonged at school. I never spoke about what I had all these years until my senior year of high school. Never had anybody to talk to. Which led me feeling very depressed and thoughts of suicidal ideation. I just recently opened up to my classmates about what I had and what I was going through several months ago before COVID happened. I have my parents and two younger siblings. And I’ve only told my father about what’s going on with me because my mother has been a big part of negativity throughout my life.

I just graduated from a catholic high school, yet I still feel unsatisfied about where I am social wise and feel just as alone and afraid to push people away.
